$comment: Hosts the deployed web app may contact, by network purpose (NetPurpose in web/src/security/net.ts, the only module that calls fetch). Each value is an array of entries: "self" for the app's own origin, or a bare origin such as "https://example.org". An empty array means the app contacts no fixed host for that purpose. Hosts the user enters (a provider endpoint, an MCP server, a sync relay) are not fixed and are not listed; net.ts still requires HTTPS or the loopback for them and shows each one in the transparency panel. Adding a host here is a reviewed change.

$purposes.app: The app's own files: the shell, its chunks, the manifest, the service worker and its precache.
$purposes.provider: Placeholder: fixed model provider endpoints, if a default is ever shipped. User-entered endpoints are not listed.
$purposes.mcp: Placeholder: fixed MCP servers. User-added servers are not listed.
$purposes.sync: Placeholder: fixed relays for end-to-end encrypted sync. Carries ciphertext only.
$purposes.download: Placeholder: pinned, hash-checked downloads such as in-browser model weights or runtimes.
$purposes.catalog: Placeholder: the model catalog the app refreshes, if it is fetched rather than bundled.
